findings.claim: No build task and no operator-only action covers DNS for the goal's public URL, so the plan can be written without anything that makes https://meet.know-me.tools resolve to the cluster.
findings.evidence: Goal 1 requires the release at https://meet.know-me.tools; the analysis states "The deployment work from the assessment (image, manifests, DNS, TLS, pipeline) is unchanged and still required" (line 28) and Risk 6 only says "the HTTPRoute hostname needs review before it is applied", yet the complete "Build required" list (items 1-7: ports, adapter, token service, room wiring, guest path, Dockerfiles/Kustomize/Argo/workflow, hosted checks) contains no DNS task, and the "Operator-only actions" list (gcloud auth, Secret creation, pinning, Argo connection, GHCR visibility, PR merges) has no DNS record creation or verification action.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit build item or operator-only action: verify or create the DNS record pointing meet.know-me.tools at the Gateway load balancer, and confirm it in the hosted checks before TLS issuance is attempted.

findings.claim: The adopted secret-handling decision and the adopted proof design contradict each other on whether the LIVEKIT secret reaches the test runner, and the analysis never resolves it.
findings.evidence: G9's adopted cand-016 row states "Nothing secret enters the repo, the image or the CI system", while cand-019's adopted risk in library-candidates.json states "A real-service check uses LiveKit Cloud minutes and needs the secret available to the test runner"; G10 requires exercising the token service "against the real LiveKit project" without saying where that check runs or how it authenticates.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the real-service check either runs against the deployed public token endpoint (no secret needed anywhere) or runs agent-side in an operator-authenticated shell, and reword cand-019's risk so it no longer contradicts cand-016's rationale.

findings.claim: The G5 adopt verdict for static-web-server is issued with coverage 0.9 while the capability the whole serving design depends on (SPA fallback and header configuration) is explicitly unread from its documentation.
findings.evidence: G5 row: "Its SPA-fallback and header options were not read from its docs in this session; confirm them at spec time"; library-candidates.json gives cand-008 coverage_estimate 0.9 on the strength of a single releases-API lookup ("gh api: latest release v2.44.2"), and 'spec time' arrives after the plan locks the serving choice.
findings.suggested_fix: Read static-web-server's SPA-fallback and header docs before the plan adopts G5, or lower the coverage estimate and name services/bff-adjacent fallback candidates so the plan carries a contingent serving decision.

findings.claim: A8's recommended default (a pull request bumps the image tag) does not satisfy the assessment's VS-C requirement, yet the analysis claims A5-A9 "do not block" and the plan can carry the defaults.
findings.evidence: "the assessment's VS-C ('merge to main and it is live with no manual steps') needs something to move the image tag. The simplest honest version is a pull request that bumps the tag" (a manual step per merge) versus the closing claim "A5 to A9 do not block: the plan can carry the recommended defaults" — and the fully automatic options (Arggo CD Image Updater, CI commit to main) are listed under "Not researched".
findings.suggested_fix: Mark A8 as an operator decision that either accepts a documented VS-C deviation or triggers research into Image Updater / CI-commit promotion, instead of letting the plan silently carry a default that fails VS-C.

findings.claim: The repo already contains site publishing scripts that the G5/G8 evaluation never considers, leaving an existing delivery category unexamined.
findings.evidence: file_tree lists ./scripts/build-site.sh, ./scripts/publish-ipfs.sh and ./scripts/publish-pages.sh, but the G5 and G8 candidate tables contain no entry for them and the "Not researched" list (Argo CD Image Updater, Sealed Secrets installation, LiveKit Cloud pricing, static-web-server configuration) does not mention them either.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a verdict row (likely reject/adapt) for the existing publish scripts stating what they publish (e.g. the design prototype) and why they are not the release delivery path, so the plan inherits an explicit rejection rather than silence.

findings.claim: The abuse controls for the public token endpoint are declared the hard part of G2 but default to hand-rolled build work with no library or pattern candidate evaluated for any of them.
findings.evidence: "Its abuse controls are the hard part, not the token: see Risks" and Risk 1 lists "a per-IP rate limit, and an `Origin` check" as controls to specify, yet no candidate in library-candidates.json addresses rate limiting or any other abuse control for the Axum service.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate at least the rate-limiting category (e.g. tower-based rate-limit middleware for Axum) as a candidate, or record in build item 3 why the controls are hand-rolled.

findings.claim: The Tier 3 research budget cap was exceeded by 2 lookups (10 against a cap of 8), a self-reported process breach.
findings.evidence: research_budget: "max_queries_per_tier": 8 with queries_used.tier3 = 10 and note "Tier 3 exceeded the cap by 2 lookups across three batched commands."
findings.suggested_fix: No content change needed; record the overage as a process deviation so the cap is enforced or renegotiated in the next phase.

findings.claim: The sole automated proof of the release's core user operation (G10) rests on a Playwright/Chromium capability that was not verified against the repo's pinned Playwright version.
findings.evidence: cand-019 is adopted as the entire G10 mechanism while its own risk states "Chromium fake-device flags were not verified against the repo's Playwright version in this session."
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the fake-device launch flags against the repo's Playwright version as an early plan-time task, and record a fallback (e.g. real capture devices on an agent-run machine) if unsupported.
